6e66e188.title: 61 Seats: Israel Election, Netanyahu, Knesset #Shorts
6e66e188.summary: This Short broke out because people were searching for the Israeli election, not because the Shorts feed pushed it. Of 51 tracked views, 48 came from YouTube search. It went out at 10:58 IST on 27 Oct 2026, about 07:30 in Israel, right as polls opened for an election covered worldwide. Its title held the exact words people typed: Israel Election, Netanyahu, Knesset, 61 seats.
6e66e188.report:
## The numbers
- **Views:** 55 against a usual 5.5, about 10x. The only other Short in the list that comes close is the Alaska megatsunami one (38 views, no #Shorts tag). The other 17 got 0 to 13 views.
- **Likes and comments:** 1 like, so about 1.8 likes per 100 views. Across the other 18 videos in the list, likes total 0, so the Israel Short has the channel's only like. It got 0 comments. The analytics row shows 0 in the last two columns, which are probably shares and subscribers gained (guess).
- **Retention:** the analytics totals read 51 views, 17.14 and 15. 51 × 17.14 s ≈ 14.6 minutes, which matches the 15, so the 17.14 is almost certainly average view duration in seconds and the 15 is minutes watched. If the Short runs about 55 s (guess, no script or length given), viewers watched about 30% of it. That is ordinary. Retention did not drive this breakout.
- **Traffic:** YouTube search 48 (94%), Shorts feed 3, other 0. This is the key fact.
- **What the numbers can't tell yet:** there is no country data and no length or retention curve. There are also no search terms, so we can't tell whether people searched "Israel election", "Netanyahu" or "61 seats". We can't compare this with what other channels' Israel Shorts got either, because the search budget ran out before I could check. Pull the search-terms report in YouTube Studio.

## Hook and first 2 seconds
The script was not provided. With 3 Shorts-feed views, the hook was barely tested in the swipe feed. People who arrive from search have already chosen the topic, so the opening only has to confirm they found the right video. A 17 s average suggests it did that and then lost them, roughly at the coalition-rules part (guess). The '61 Seats' number in the title probably worked as the promise: one number that explains the whole election.

## Psychology
- **Main draw (guess):** the urge to understand an event everyone was talking about that day. The question was "what does it take to win in Israel?"
- **Curiosity gap:** "why neither bloc reaches it" leaves the question open, and 'what happens next' gives a payoff.
- **Why so few likes, comments and shares:** search viewers want a fact and leave. Israel is a polarising topic, and a neutral explainer gives people nothing to argue with or take sides on.

## Topic and timing
- **The event:** Israel elected all 120 Knesset seats on 27 Oct 2026. Outlets including the Library of Congress, Times of Israel, Haaretz and CNN had flagged the date for weeks. It was also the first election since 7 Oct 2023, which raised interest around the world.
- **Timing:** publishing at 10:58 IST put the Short live before the day's peak search demand. That covers polls opening in Israel, Europe waking up, and the US and UK checking news through the day, plus exit polls at night. The Lula, Surrey and Jamia Shorts covered events whose search peak had already passed or was small.
- **The framing held up:** the Jerusalem Post later reported Netanyahu's bloc at about 53 seats and the opposition at 48. ABC reported the bloc kept its lead but had no majority. 'Neither bloc reaches 61' turned out right, so the Short stayed relevant after results came in.
- **Countries:** no data. I'd guess the US, UK and India, plus some Israel.

## Title, description and thumbnail
- **Title:** '61 Seats: Israel Election, Netanyahu, Knesset' is built like a list of search keywords: a country, an event, a leader, an institution.
- **Compare 'Lost to a List With No Leader':** '14 Years in Power, Lost to a List With No Leader' names no country or person, so nobody can find it by search (5 views).
- **Compare 'Lula Wins Brazil':** it named the person but was published after the result, at 00:32 IST (6 views).
- **Description:** it repeats the key terms (Knesset, 120 seats, 61, Oct 7) and has a #IsraelElection hashtag. Most other Shorts use generic hashtags only (guess, based on this template).
- **Thumbnail:** Shorts thumbnails matter little in search. Not judged.

## Audience and algorithm
- **Who and how:** it reached people outside the channel through search. This is a channel with almost no subscribers and no feed pull. Search is the one door a new channel can open without history, because ranking follows how well a video matches the query and how fresh it is, not subscriber count.
- **Feed did nothing:** the Shorts feed tried 3 times and stopped. The ~30% view percentage (guess) and zero shares gave it no signal to grow.
- **No outside sharing:** external traffic was 0.

## What did not matter
- **A number at the start of the title:** nearly every other Short starts with one, and they got 0 to 13 views.
- **The AI hosts and stock footage:** they are the same on every Short.
- **How heavy the news is:** the Houthi/Ras Tanura (11) and Spain crash (5) Shorts were serious too.
- **Likes and comments:** 1 like and no comments, so they did not drive anything.

## Repeat this
1. Choose a scheduled world event with global search demand on the day (an election, a central bank decision, a launch).
2. Publish before or as it starts, not after the result.
3. Put the exact search words in the title: country + event + leader + institution, led by a key number.
4. Frame it as how it works and what happens next, so it stays true whatever the result.

## Test next
- **Follow-ups:** after a preview Short, publish a same-pattern results Short within 12 hours, e.g. '53 vs 48: Israel Election Result, Netanyahu, Eisenkot'.
- **Search titles on non-election news:** check whether keyword titles also win search for other scheduled events, such as the Japan rate decision ('Bank of Japan Rate Decision, 1.25%, Yen').
- **Retention:** show the main number in the first 2 seconds, and keep the explanation under 40 s, to see if average view duration rises above 17 s.
- **Engagement:** end with a neutral question that invites a prediction, to see if comments appear.

changes.rule: Each day, choose at least one Short about a scheduled global event that happens within the next 24 hours and that people worldwide will search for by name, such as a national election, a central bank decision or a big launch.

Write titles as a key number followed by 2-3 exact search terms people would type: country + event + leader or institution (pattern: '61 Seats: Israel Election, Netanyahu, Knesset'). Never publish a title that leaves out the country or the main person's name.
Start the first line of the description with the main search phrase (e.g. 'Israel election 2026 explained'), and add one hashtag specific to the event (e.g. #IsraelElection) next to #Shorts.

In the first sentence, name the event and its key number to confirm the viewer found the right video ('Israel needs 61 of 120 seats to govern'), then explain what happens next, and finish within 40 seconds.
Put the key number on screen as a large graphic (e.g. a 61-of-120 seat bar) within the first 2 seconds, and change the visual every 2-3 seconds after that.
For every scheduled event covered with a preview Short, also publish a results Short with the same title pattern and the actual result numbers within 12 hours of the result.
